class ConnectionState(Enum):
    """Connection lifecycle state for ``StatsClient``.

    Attributes:
        DISCONNECTED: No active TCP session is open.
        CONNECTING: TCP handshake is in progress.
        CONNECTED: TCP session is established and reading events.
        FAILED: Reconnect attempts were exhausted.
    """

    DISCONNECTED = "disconnected"
    CONNECTING = "connecting"
    CONNECTED = "connected"
    FAILED = "failed"

class StatsClient:
    """Async event client for the local Rocket League Stats API TCP stream."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        host: str = "127.0.0.1",
        port: int = 49123,
        reconnect: bool = True,
        reconnect_delay: float = 0.5,
        max_reconnect_delay: float = 30.0,
        max_reconnect_attempts: int | None = None,
        include_raw: bool = False,
        queue_size: int = 2048,
        overflow: Literal["block", "drop", "raise"] = "block",
        connect_timeout: float = 5.0,
        drain_on_disconnect: bool = False,
        handler_timeout: float | None = None,
        track_state: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the client configuration without opening a socket.

        Args:
            host: Stats API host address.
            port: Stats API TCP port in the range 1..65535.
            reconnect: Whether to reconnect automatically when the socket closes.
            reconnect_delay: Initial backoff delay in seconds before reconnecting.
            max_reconnect_delay: Maximum backoff delay in seconds between attempts.
            max_reconnect_attempts: Maximum reconnect attempts before entering
                ``ConnectionState.FAILED``. ``None`` retries indefinitely.
            include_raw: Attach the raw JSON string to ``EventMessage.raw``.
            queue_size: Maximum number of events buffered in the internal queue.
            overflow: Queue-full policy: ``"block"`` waits when an ``events()``
                consumer is active (or evicts the oldest item when no iterator is
                attached), ``"drop"`` discards incoming queue items, and
                ``"raise"`` raises ``asyncio.QueueFull``.
            connect_timeout: Seconds to wait for the TCP handshake.
            drain_on_disconnect: Clear queued events when ``disconnect()`` runs.
            handler_timeout: Maximum seconds an awaitable handler may run before
                being cancelled. ``None`` disables the timeout.
            track_state: Update ``client.state`` on incoming events.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If any numeric bound or ``overflow`` mode is invalid.
        """
        _validate_client_options(
            port=port,
            reconnect_delay=reconnect_delay,
            max_reconnect_delay=max_reconnect_delay,
            max_reconnect_attempts=max_reconnect_attempts,
            queue_size=queue_size,
            overflow=overflow,
            connect_timeout=connect_timeout,
            handler_timeout=handler_timeout,
        )

        self.host = host
        self.port = port
        self.reconnect = reconnect
        self.reconnect_delay = reconnect_delay
        self.max_reconnect_delay = max_reconnect_delay
        self.max_reconnect_attempts = max_reconnect_attempts
        self.include_raw = include_raw
        self.connect_timeout = connect_timeout
        self.overflow = overflow
        self.drain_on_disconnect = drain_on_disconnect
        self.handler_timeout = handler_timeout
        self.track_state = track_state

        self._queue: asyncio.Queue[EventMessage] = asyncio.Queue(maxsize=queue_size)
        self._event_consumers = 0
        self._handlers_by_event: dict[str, list[_AnyCallable]] = defaultdict(list)
        self._handlers_any: list[_AnyCallable] = []
        self._on_connect_handlers: list[_SimpleHandler] = []
        self._on_disconnect_handlers: list[_SimpleHandler] = []
        self._error_handlers: list[_ErrorHandler] = []
        self._logger = logging.getLogger("rlstatsapi")

        self._reader: asyncio.StreamReader | None = None
        self._writer: asyncio.StreamWriter | None = None
        self._reader_task: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None
        self._stopping = False
        self._connection_state = ConnectionState.DISCONNECTED
        self._permanently_failed = False
        self._last_error: Exception | None = None
        self._metrics = ClientMetrics()
        self._state_tracker = MatchStateTracker()

    @property
    def connection_state(self) -> ConnectionState:
        """Current connection lifecycle state."""
        return self._connection_state

    @property
    def is_connected(self) -> bool:
        """``True`` when the TCP connection is established."""
        return self._connection_state == ConnectionState.CONNECTED

    @property
    def metrics(self) -> ClientMetrics:
        """Counters for throughput, drops, errors, and reconnects."""
        return self._metrics

    @property
    def state(self) -> MatchStateSnapshot:
        """Latest match snapshot derived from incoming events."""
        return self._state_tracker.snapshot

    @property
    def last_error(self) -> Exception | None:
        """Latest connection or stream error recorded by the reader task."""
        return self._last_error

    @property
    def permanently_failed(self) -> bool:
        """``True`` when ``max_reconnect_attempts`` was exhausted."""
        return self._permanently_failed

    async def __aenter__(self) -> StatsClient:
        """Start the background reader task upon entering the context manager.

        Returns:
            StatsClient: This client instance.
        """
        await self.connect()
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, *_: object) -> None:
        """Stop the reader task and close the socket on context exit."""
        await self.disconnect()

    async def connect(self) -> None:
        """Start the background reader task if it is not already running."""
        if self._reader_task and not self._reader_task.done():
            self._logger.debug("connect() ignored: reader already running")
            return

        self._stopping = False
        self._permanently_failed = False
        self._last_error = None
        self._reader_task = asyncio.create_task(self._run(), name="rlstatsapi-reader")
        self._logger.debug("reader task started")

    async def disconnect(self, timeout: float = 5.0) -> None:
        """Close the active socket and stop the background reader task.

        Args:
            timeout: Maximum seconds to wait for the reader task to finish.
        """
        self._stopping = True
        self._logger.debug("disconnect requested")

        close_timeout = min(timeout, 1.0) if timeout > 0 else 0.1
        await self._close_writer(timeout=close_timeout)

        if self._reader_task is not None:
            self._reader_task.cancel()
            with contextlib.suppress(asyncio.TimeoutError, asyncio.CancelledError):
                await asyncio.wait_for(self._reader_task, timeout=timeout)
            self._reader_task = None

        if self._connection_state != ConnectionState.FAILED:
            self._connection_state = ConnectionState.DISCONNECTED

        if self.drain_on_disconnect:
            self.clear_queue()
        self._logger.debug("disconnected")

    def on_connect(self, handler: _SimpleHandler) -> None:
        """Register a callback invoked after the TCP connection is established."""
        self._on_connect_handlers.append(handler)

    def off_connect(self, handler: _SimpleHandler) -> None:
        """Unregister a callback previously added with ``on_connect``."""
        with contextlib.suppress(ValueError):
            self._on_connect_handlers.remove(handler)

    def on_disconnect(self, handler: _SimpleHandler) -> None:
        """Register a callback invoked when an established TCP session closes."""
        self._on_disconnect_handlers.append(handler)

    def off_disconnect(self, handler: _SimpleHandler) -> None:
        """Unregister a callback previously added with ``on_disconnect``."""
        with contextlib.suppress(ValueError):
            self._on_disconnect_handlers.remove(handler)

    def on_handler_error(self, handler: _ErrorHandler) -> None:
        """Register a callback invoked when an event handler raises an exception."""
        self._error_handlers.append(handler)

    def off_handler_error(self, handler: _ErrorHandler) -> None:
        """Unregister a callback previously added with ``on_handler_error``."""
        with contextlib.suppress(ValueError):
            self._error_handlers.remove(handler)

    def on(self, event_name: str, handler: _AnyCallable | None = None) -> Any:
        """Register an event handler directly or return a decorator.

        Args:
            event_name: Rocket League event name (such as ``"GoalScored"``).
            handler: Callback to register. When omitted, returns a decorator
                that registers the decorated function and returns it unchanged.

        Returns:
            Callable | None: The decorator function when ``handler`` is ``None``,
            otherwise ``None``.
        """
        if handler is None:

            def decorator(h: _AnyCallable) -> _AnyCallable:
                self._handlers_by_event[event_name].append(h)
                return h

            return decorator
        self._handlers_by_event[event_name].append(handler)
        return None

    def on_any(self, handler: Handler) -> None:
        """Register a global handler invoked for every incoming event."""
        self._handlers_any.append(handler)

    def on_many(self, event_names: Iterable[str], handler: Handler) -> None:
        """Register the same handler for multiple event names."""
        for event_name in event_names:
            self._handlers_by_event[event_name].append(handler)

    def off(self, event_name: str, handler: _AnyCallable) -> None:
        """Unregister a handler for a specific event if present."""
        handlers = self._handlers_by_event.get(event_name)
        if handlers:
            with contextlib.suppress(ValueError):
                handlers.remove(handler)
            if not handlers:
                self._handlers_by_event.pop(event_name, None)

    def off_any(self, handler: _AnyCallable) -> None:
        """Unregister a global handler previously added with ``on_any``."""
        with contextlib.suppress(ValueError):
            self._handlers_any.remove(handler)

    def clear_queue(self) -> None:
        """Discard all pending events currently buffered in the internal queue."""
        while True:
            try:
                self._queue.get_nowait()
            except asyncio.QueueEmpty:
                break

    def once(self, event_name: str, handler: _AnyCallable) -> None:
        """Register a handler that executes on the next matching event and removes itself."""

        async def wrapper(msg: EventMessage) -> None:
            self.off(event_name, wrapper)
            result = handler(msg)
            if result is not None and inspect.isawaitable(result):
                await result

        self._handlers_by_event[event_name].append(wrapper)

    async def events(self, *event_names: str) -> AsyncIterator[EventMessage]:
        """Yield incoming events from the internal queue, optionally filtered by name.

        Args:
            *event_names: Optional event names to filter by.

        Yields:
            EventMessage: Next matching event from the stream.
        """
        filters = frozenset(event_names)
        self._event_consumers += 1
        try:
            while True:
                message = await self._queue.get()
                if not filters or message.event in filters:
                    yield message
        finally:
            self._event_consumers -= 1

    async def wait_for(
        self,
        event_name: str,
        *,
        timeout: float | None = None,
    ) -> EventMessage:
        """Wait for the next occurrence of ``event_name`` and return its message.

        Args:
            event_name: Event name to wait for (for example ``"GoalScored"``).
            timeout: Maximum seconds to wait before raising ``asyncio.TimeoutError``.

        Returns:
            EventMessage: The first matching event received after registration.

        Raises:
            asyncio.TimeoutError: If ``timeout`` elapses before the event arrives.
        """
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        future: asyncio.Future[EventMessage] = loop.create_future()

        def _handler(msg: EventMessage) -> None:
            if not future.done():
                future.set_result(msg)

        self._handlers_by_event[event_name].append(_handler)
        try:
            return await asyncio.wait_for(future, timeout=timeout)
        finally:
            self.off(event_name, _handler)

    async def send_command(

        data: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:

        The game does not acknowledge commands. Watch the event stream to see
        the effect (for example ``MatchPaused`` after ``SetMatchPaused``).

        Args:
            command: Envelope built by ``rlstatsapi.commands`` or a command name.
            data: Wire-format variables when ``command`` is a name.

        Raises:
            InvalidCommandError: If the game would reject the command.
            ConnectionError: If the client is not connected.
        """
        payload = encode_command(
            build_command(command, data) if isinstance(command, str) else command
        )
        writer = self._writer
        if writer is None or self._connection_state != ConnectionState.CONNECTED:
            raise ConnectionError("StatsClient is not connected")
        writer.write(payload)
        await writer.drain()

    async def _close_writer(self, timeout: float = 1.0) -> None:
        """Close the active ``StreamWriter`` and bound ``wait_closed`` by ``timeout``."""
        writer = self._writer
        self._writer = None
        self._reader = None
        if writer is None:
            return
        with contextlib.suppress(OSError, asyncio.TimeoutError, asyncio.CancelledError):
            writer.close()
            await asyncio.wait_for(writer.wait_closed(), timeout=timeout)

    async def _run(self) -> None:
        """Manage the TCP connection lifecycle, reconnect backoff, and read loop."""
        attempt = 0
        while not self._stopping:
            try:
                self._logger.debug("connecting to tcp://%s:%d", self.host, self.port)
                self._connection_state = ConnectionState.CONNECTING
                self._reader, self._writer = await asyncio.wait_for(
                    asyncio.open_connection(host=self.host, port=self.port),
                    timeout=self.connect_timeout,
                )
                self._connection_state = ConnectionState.CONNECTED
                attempt = 0
                self._logger.debug("tcp socket connected")
                await self._fire_simple(self._on_connect_handlers)
                await self._read_loop(self._reader)
            except asyncio.CancelledError:
                self._logger.debug("reader task cancelled")
                raise
            except Exception as exc:
                self._last_error = exc
                self._metrics.connection_failures += 1
                self._logger.debug("connection/read error: %s", exc)
                if not self.reconnect or self._stopping:
                    self._logger.debug(
                        "stopping reader (reconnect disabled or stopping)"
                    )
                    return
                attempt += 1
                self._metrics.reconnect_count += 1
                if (
                    self.max_reconnect_attempts is not None
                    and attempt > self.max_reconnect_attempts
                ):
                    self._permanently_failed = True
                    self._connection_state = ConnectionState.FAILED
                    self._logger.debug(
                        "max reconnect attempts (%d) reached",
                        self.max_reconnect_attempts,
                    )
                    return
                await self._cleanup_session()
                delay = min(
                    self.reconnect_delay * (2 ** (attempt - 1)),
                    self.max_reconnect_delay,
                ) * random.uniform(0.75, 1.25)
                self._logger.debug("reconnecting in %.2fs (attempt %d)", delay, attempt)
                await asyncio.sleep(delay)
            finally:
                await self._cleanup_session()

    async def _cleanup_session(self) -> None:
        """Reset connection state, fire disconnect handlers if needed, and close writer."""
        was_connected = self._connection_state == ConnectionState.CONNECTED
        if self._connection_state != ConnectionState.FAILED:
            self._connection_state = ConnectionState.DISCONNECTED
        if was_connected:
            await self._fire_simple(self._on_disconnect_handlers)
        if self._writer is not None:
            await self._close_writer()
            self._logger.debug("tcp socket closed")

    def _enqueue_nowait(self, message: EventMessage) -> bool:
        """Queue ``message`` without awaiting. Return ``False`` if the caller must block."""
        queue = self._queue
        overflow = self.overflow
        if overflow == "block":
            if queue.full():
                if self._event_consumers > 0:
                    return False
                with contextlib.suppress(asyncio.QueueEmpty):
                    queue.get_nowait()
            queue.put_nowait(message)
        elif overflow == "drop":
            if queue.full():
                self._metrics.dropped_events += 1
                self._logger.warning("queue full, dropping %s event", message.event)
                return True
            queue.put_nowait(message)
        else:
            queue.put_nowait(message)
        self._metrics.queued_events += 1
        return True

    async def _enqueue_message(self, message: EventMessage) -> None:
        """Push ``message`` into the internal queue according to ``self.overflow``."""
        if not self._enqueue_nowait(message):
            await self._queue.put(message)
            self._metrics.queued_events += 1

    async def _read_loop(self, reader: asyncio.StreamReader) -> None:
        """Read chunks from the TCP stream, decode JSON frames, and dispatch events."""
        read = reader.read
        consume = self._consume
        pending = b""
        while not self._stopping:
            chunk = await read(_READ_CHUNK_SIZE)
            if not chunk:
                raise ConnectionAbortedError("Socket closed by peer")
            pending = await consume(pending + chunk if pending else chunk)

    def _accept(self, decoded: Any, frame: bytes | str) -> EventMessage | None:
        """Build the message for one decoded frame and update metrics and state."""
        if type(decoded) is not dict:
            self._logger.debug("ignored invalid message (json/envelope)")
            return None
        event = decoded.get("Event")
        data = decoded.get("Data")
        if type(data) is str and len(data) <= _MAX_JSON_FIELD_BYTES:
            try:
                data = _JSON_LOADS(data)
            except ValueError:
                data = None
        if type(event) is not str or type(data) is not dict:
            self._logger.debug("ignored invalid message (json/envelope)")
            return None

        raw: str | None = None
        if self.include_raw:
            raw = frame if type(frame) is str else frame.decode("utf-8", "replace")  # type: ignore[union-attr]
        message = EventMessage(event, data, raw)
        self._metrics.received_events += 1
        if self.track_state:
            self._state_tracker.ingest(message)
        return message

    def _needs_await(self, message: EventMessage) -> bool:
        """Queue ``message`` if nothing has to be awaited; otherwise return ``True``."""
        if self._handlers_any or self._handlers_by_event.get(message.event):
            return True
        return not self._enqueue_nowait(message)

    async def _deliver(self, message: EventMessage) -> None:
        """Run handlers for ``message`` and then queue it."""
        await self._dispatch(message)
        await self._enqueue_message(message)

    async def _consume(self, data: bytes) -> bytes:  # pylint: disable=too-many-locals
        """Decode every complete JSON message in ``data`` and return the leftover bytes.

        This is the hot path. A read usually holds exactly one message, so the
        whole chunk is parsed first. Otherwise it is split at message
        boundaries, and anything unusual goes through ``_consume_slow``.
        """
        loads = _JSON_LOADS
        accept = self._accept
        needs_await = self._needs_await

        # Only a chunk ending in ``}`` or whitespace can be one whole message.
        tail = data[-1]
        if tail == _CLOSE_BRACE or tail <= 0x20:
            try:
                decoded = loads(data)
            except ValueError:
                pass
            else:
                message = accept(decoded, data)
                if message is not None and needs_await(message):
                    await self._deliver(message)
                return b""

        # Frame ``data`` at each boundary; the last frame runs to the end.
        starts = [0]
        ends = []
        for match in _FRAME_BOUNDARY_RE.finditer(data):
            ends.append(match.start() + 1)
            starts.append(match.end() - 2)
        ends.append(len(data))
        last = len(ends) - 1
        remainder = b""
        for index, start in enumerate(starts):
            frame = data[start : ends[index]] if last else data
            if (
                index == last
                and frame[0] == _OPEN_BRACE
                and frame.rstrip()[-1] != _CLOSE_BRACE
            ):
                remainder = frame  # incomplete message, wait for more bytes
                break
            try:
                decoded = loads(frame)
            except ValueError:
                leftover = await self._consume_slow(frame)
                if index == last:
                    remainder = leftover
                continue
            message = accept(decoded, frame)
            if message is not None and needs_await(message):
                await self._deliver(message)

        if len(remainder) > _MAX_BUFFER_BYTES:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Stream buffer exceeded {_MAX_BUFFER_BYTES} bytes without a complete JSON object"
            )
        return remainder

    async def _consume_slow(self, data: bytes) -> bytes:
        """Tolerant decoder for data the fast path rejected.

        Handles leading garbage, invalid UTF-8 (replaced with U+FFFD) and
        messages split in the middle of a multibyte character.
        """
        head, tail = _split_incomplete_utf8(data)
        try:
            text = head.decode("utf-8")
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            text = head.decode("utf-8", "replace")
            self._logger.warning("received invalid UTF-8 bytes; replaced with U+FFFD")

        raw_decode = json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode
        text_len = len(text)
        pos = 0
        while pos < text_len:
            if text[pos] != "{":
                match = _WHITESPACE_RE.match(text, pos)
                if match is not None:
                    pos = match.end()
                if pos >= text_len:
                    break
                if text[pos] != "{":
                    pos = text.find("{", pos)
                    if pos == -1:
                        pos = text_len
                        break
            try:
                decoded, end_idx = raw_decode(text, pos)
            except _JSON_DECODE_ERROR:
                break
            message = self._accept(decoded, text[pos:end_idx])
            pos = end_idx
            if message is not None and self._needs_await(message):
                await self._deliver(message)

        return (text[pos:].encode("utf-8") if pos < text_len else b"") + tail

    async def _dispatch(self, message: EventMessage) -> None:
        """Dispatch ``message`` to global handlers and event-specific handlers."""
        any_handlers = self._handlers_any
        event_handlers = self._handlers_by_event.get(message.event)
        if not any_handlers and not event_handlers:
            return

        handlers: tuple[_AnyCallable, ...] = (
            (*any_handlers, *event_handlers)
            if (any_handlers and event_handlers)
            else tuple(any_handlers or event_handlers or ())
        )

        timeout = self.handler_timeout
        for handler in handlers:
            try:
                result = handler(message)
                if result is not None and inspect.isawaitable(result):
                    if timeout is not None:
                        await asyncio.wait_for(result, timeout=timeout)
                    else:
                        await result
            except Exception as exc:
                await self._handle_dispatch_error(message, exc, handler)

    async def _handle_dispatch_error(
        self, message: EventMessage, exc: Exception, handler: _AnyCallable
    ) -> None:
        """Record a handler error and notify registered error callbacks."""
        self._metrics.handler_errors += 1
        if not self._error_handlers:
            self._logger.error("handler error for %s: %s", message.event, exc)
            return

        for error_handler in tuple(self._error_handlers):
            try:
                err_result = error_handler(message, exc, handler)
                if err_result is not None and inspect.isawaitable(err_result):
                    await err_result
            except Exception as err_exc:
                self._logger.error("error handler itself raised: %s", err_exc)

    async def _fire_simple(self, handlers: list[_SimpleHandler]) -> None:
        """Invoke connection lifecycle callbacks and await coroutine results."""
        for handler in tuple(handlers):
            try:
                result = handler()
                if result is not None and inspect.isawaitable(result):
                    await result
            except Exception as exc:
                self._logger.error("lifecycle handler error: %s", exc)

    self,
    host: str = "127.0.0.1",
    port: int = 49123,
    reconnect: bool = True,
    reconnect_delay: float = 0.5,
    max_reconnect_delay: float = 30.0,
    max_reconnect_attempts: int | None = None,
    include_raw: bool = False,
    queue_size: int = 2048,

    connect_timeout: float = 5.0,
    drain_on_disconnect: bool = False,
    handler_timeout: float | None = None,
    track_state: bool = True,
) -> None:
    """Initialize the client configuration without opening a socket.

    Args:
        host: Stats API host address.
        port: Stats API TCP port in the range 1..65535.
        reconnect: Whether to reconnect automatically when the socket closes.
        reconnect_delay: Initial backoff delay in seconds before reconnecting.
        max_reconnect_delay: Maximum backoff delay in seconds between attempts.
        max_reconnect_attempts: Maximum reconnect attempts before entering
            ``ConnectionState.FAILED``. ``None`` retries indefinitely.
        include_raw: Attach the raw JSON string to ``EventMessage.raw``.
        queue_size: Maximum number of events buffered in the internal queue.
        overflow: Queue-full policy: ``"block"`` waits when an ``events()``
            consumer is active (or evicts the oldest item when no iterator is
            attached), ``"drop"`` discards incoming queue items, and
            ``"raise"`` raises ``asyncio.QueueFull``.
        connect_timeout: Seconds to wait for the TCP handshake.
        drain_on_disconnect: Clear queued events when ``disconnect()`` runs.
        handler_timeout: Maximum seconds an awaitable handler may run before
            being cancelled. ``None`` disables the timeout.

        ValueError: If any numeric bound or ``overflow`` mode is invalid.

        port=port,
        reconnect_delay=reconnect_delay,
        max_reconnect_delay=max_reconnect_delay,
        max_reconnect_attempts=max_reconnect_attempts,
        queue_size=queue_size,
        overflow=overflow,
        connect_timeout=connect_timeout,
        handler_timeout=handler_timeout,
    )

    self.host = host
    self.port = port
    self.reconnect = reconnect
    self.reconnect_delay = reconnect_delay
    self.max_reconnect_delay = max_reconnect_delay
    self.max_reconnect_attempts = max_reconnect_attempts
    self.include_raw = include_raw
    self.connect_timeout = connect_timeout
    self.overflow = overflow
    self.drain_on_disconnect = drain_on_disconnect

    self._queue: asyncio.Queue[EventMessage] = asyncio.Queue(maxsize=queue_size)

    self._handlers_by_event: dict[str, list[_AnyCallable]] = defaultdict(list)
    self._handlers_any: list[_AnyCallable] = []
    self._on_connect_handlers: list[_SimpleHandler] = []
    self._on_disconnect_handlers: list[_SimpleHandler] = []
    self._error_handlers: list[_ErrorHandler] = []
    self._logger = logging.getLogger("rlstatsapi")

    self._reader: asyncio.StreamReader | None = None
    self._writer: asyncio.StreamWriter | None = None
    self._reader_task: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None

    self._connection_state = ConnectionState.DISCONNECTED

async def disconnect(self, timeout: float = 5.0) -> None:
    """Close the active socket and stop the background reader task.

    Args:
        timeout: Maximum seconds to wait for the reader task to finish.
    """
    self._stopping = True
    self._logger.debug("disconnect requested")

    close_timeout = min(timeout, 1.0) if timeout > 0 else 0.1
    await self._close_writer(timeout=close_timeout)

    if self._reader_task is not None:
        self._reader_task.cancel()
        with contextlib.suppress(asyncio.TimeoutError, asyncio.CancelledError):
            await asyncio.wait_for(self._reader_task, timeout=timeout)
        self._reader_task = None

    if self._connection_state != ConnectionState.FAILED:
        self._connection_state = ConnectionState.DISCONNECTED

    if self.drain_on_disconnect:
        self.clear_queue()

async def events(self, *event_names: str) -> AsyncIterator[EventMessage]:
    """Yield incoming events from the internal queue, optionally filtered by name.

    Args:
        *event_names: Optional event names to filter by.

    Yields:
        EventMessage: Next matching event from the stream.
    """
    filters = frozenset(event_names)
    self._event_consumers += 1
    try:
        while True:
            message = await self._queue.get()
            if not filters or message.event in filters:
                yield message
    finally:
        self._event_consumers -= 1

def on(self, event_name: str, handler: _AnyCallable | None = None) -> Any:
    """Register an event handler directly or return a decorator.

    Args:
        event_name: Rocket League event name (such as ``"GoalScored"``).
        handler: Callback to register. When omitted, returns a decorator
            that registers the decorated function and returns it unchanged.

    Returns:
        Callable | None: The decorator function when ``handler`` is ``None``,
        otherwise ``None``.
    """
    if handler is None:

        def decorator(h: _AnyCallable) -> _AnyCallable:
            self._handlers_by_event[event_name].append(h)
            return h

        return decorator
    self._handlers_by_event[event_name].append(handler)
    return None

    """
    payload = encode_command(
        build_command(command, data) if isinstance(command, str) else command
    )
    writer = self._writer
    if writer is None or self._connection_state != ConnectionState.CONNECTED:
        raise ConnectionError("StatsClient is not connected")
    writer.write(payload)
    await writer.drain()

async def wait_for(
    self,
    event_name: str,
    *,
    timeout: float | None = None,
) -> EventMessage:
    """Wait for the next occurrence of ``event_name`` and return its message.

    Args:
        event_name: Event name to wait for (for example ``"GoalScored"``).
        timeout: Maximum seconds to wait before raising ``asyncio.TimeoutError``.

    Returns:
        EventMessage: The first matching event received after registration.

    Raises:
        asyncio.TimeoutError: If ``timeout`` elapses before the event arrives.
    """
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    future: asyncio.Future[EventMessage] = loop.create_future()

    def _handler(msg: EventMessage) -> None:
        if not future.done():
            future.set_result(msg)

    self._handlers_by_event[event_name].append(_handler)
    try:
        return await asyncio.wait_for(future, timeout=timeout)
    finally:
        self.off(event_name, _handler)

def build_command(name: str, data: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None) -> Command:
    """Validate a command given by wire name and ``Data`` mapping.

    Args:
        name: Command name, one of ``COMMAND_NAMES``.
        data: Wire-format variables (for example ``{"bVisible": False}``).

    Returns:
        Command: Validated command envelope with unknown keys removed.

    Raises:
        InvalidCommandError: If the name is unknown or the data is not accepted.
    """
    data = data or {}
    if not isinstance(data, Mapping):
        raise InvalidCommandError(str(name), "Data must be an object")
    get = data.get
    if name == "ChangePOV":
        return change_pov(get("Focus"), get("Perspective"))
    if name == "LoadReplay":
        return load_replay(get("FileName"), get("Path"))
    if name == "SeekReplay":
        return seek_replay(get("Frame"), get("TimeSeconds"))
    if name == "SetGameSpeed":
        return set_game_speed(get("Speed"))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    if name == "SetHUDVisibility":
        return set_hud_visibility(get("bVisible"))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    if name == "SetMatchPaused":
        return set_match_paused(get("bPaused"))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    raise InvalidCommandError(
        str(name), f"unsupported command; expected one of {', '.join(COMMAND_NAMES)}"
    )

    perspective: Perspective | None = None,

def candidate_stats_api_paths() -> list[Path]:
    """Return candidate user paths for the Stats API config on Windows.

    In each folder ``TAStatsAPI.ini`` comes before ``DefaultStatsAPI.ini``,
    which is the order the game uses.

    Returns:
        list[Path]: Deduplicated list of candidate config paths.
    """
    roots: list[Path] = []
    for env_name in ("USERPROFILE", "HOME"):
        value = os.getenv(env_name)
        if value:
            root = Path(value).expanduser().resolve()
            if root.exists():
                roots.append(root)

    candidates: list[Path] = []
    for root in roots:
        for documents in (
            root / "Documents",
            root / "Documentos",
            root / "OneDrive" / "Documents",
            root / "OneDrive" / "Documentos",
        ):
            folder = documents / _USER_CONFIG_RELATIVE_DIR
            candidates.append(folder / DEFAULT_STATS_API_FILENAME)
            candidates.append(folder / DEFAULT_STATS_API_FALLBACK_FILENAME)

    unique: list[Path] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for path in candidates:
        key = str(path).casefold()
        if key not in seen:
            seen.add(key)
            unique.append(path)
    return unique

    web_port: int | None = None,

class MatchStateTracker:
    """Maintain a rolling summary of the active match from incoming events."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Initialize the tracker with an empty ``MatchStateSnapshot``."""
        self._snapshot = MatchStateSnapshot()
        self._pending: dict[str, Any] | None = None

    @property
    def snapshot(self) -> MatchStateSnapshot:
        """Current match snapshot, brought up to date on access."""
        pending = self._pending
        if pending is not None:
            self._pending = None
            self._apply_update_state(self._snapshot, pending)
        return self._snapshot

    def reset(self) -> None:
        """Replace the current snapshot with a fresh ``MatchStateSnapshot``."""
        self._snapshot = MatchStateSnapshot()
        self._pending = None

    def update(self, message: EventMessage) -> MatchStateSnapshot:
        """Apply one incoming event and return the updated snapshot.

        Args:
            message: Normalized event message from the stream.

        Returns:
            MatchStateSnapshot: The updated match state snapshot.
        """
        self.ingest(message)
        return self.snapshot

    def ingest(self, message: EventMessage) -> None:
        """Record one incoming event without building player snapshots yet.

        ``UpdateState`` arrives up to 120 times per second, so its payload is
        only kept here and applied when ``snapshot`` is read or another event
        that touches the state arrives.
        """
        event = message.event
        snapshot = self._snapshot
        counts = snapshot.event_counts
        if event == "UpdateState":
            snapshot.last_event = event
            counts[event] = counts.get(event, 0) + 1
            self._pending = message.data
            return

        if event == "MatchDestroyed":
            self.reset()
            snapshot = self._snapshot
            snapshot.last_event = event
            snapshot.event_counts[event] = 1
            return

        pending = self._pending
        if pending is not None:
            self._pending = None
            self._apply_update_state(snapshot, pending)

        snapshot.last_event = event
        counts[event] = counts.get(event, 0) + 1

        data = message.data
        match_guid = data.get("MatchGuid")
        if isinstance(match_guid, str) and match_guid:
            snapshot.match_guid = match_guid

        if event == "ClockUpdatedSeconds":
            self._apply_clock_updated(snapshot, data)
        elif event == "GoalScored":
            self._apply_goal_scored(snapshot, data)
        elif event == "GoalReplayStart":
            snapshot.replay_active = True
        elif event == "GoalReplayEnd":
            snapshot.replay_active = False
        elif event == "MatchEnded":
            winner_team_num = data.get("WinnerTeamNum")
            if _is_int(winner_team_num):
                snapshot.winner_team_num = winner_team_num
                snapshot.no_contest = winner_team_num == -1
            snapshot.has_winner = not snapshot.no_contest

    def _apply_update_state(
        self,
        snapshot: MatchStateSnapshot,
        data: dict[str, Any],
    ) -> None:
        """Extract game, team, and player fields from an ``UpdateState`` payload."""
        match_guid = data.get("MatchGuid")
        if isinstance(match_guid, str) and match_guid:
            snapshot.match_guid = match_guid

        game = data.get("Game")
        if not isinstance(game, dict):
            return

        self._apply_teams(snapshot, game.get("Teams"))
        self._apply_players(snapshot, data.get("Players"), game)

        time_seconds = game.get("TimeSeconds")
        if _is_int(time_seconds):
            snapshot.time_seconds = time_seconds

        snapshot.overtime = bool(game.get("bOvertime", False))
        snapshot.replay_active = bool(game.get("bReplay", False))
        snapshot.has_winner = bool(game.get("bHasWinner", False))

        playlist_id = game.get("PlaylistId")
        if _is_int(playlist_id):
            snapshot.playlist_id = playlist_id

        arena = game.get("Arena")
        if isinstance(arena, str) and arena:
            snapshot.arena = arena

        winner = game.get("Winner")
        if isinstance(winner, str) and winner:
            snapshot.winner = winner

    def _apply_clock_updated(
        self,
        snapshot: MatchStateSnapshot,
        data: dict[str, Any],
    ) -> None:
        """Update clock seconds and overtime flag from ``ClockUpdatedSeconds``."""
        time_seconds = data.get("TimeSeconds")
        if _is_int(time_seconds):
            snapshot.time_seconds = time_seconds
        if "bOvertime" in data:
            snapshot.overtime = bool(data.get("bOvertime", False))

    def _apply_teams(self, snapshot: MatchStateSnapshot, teams: object) -> None:
        """Update blue and orange scores from the ``Teams`` list."""
        if not isinstance(teams, list):
            return

        for team in teams:
            if not isinstance(team, dict):
                continue
            team_num = team.get("TeamNum")
            score = team.get("Score")
            if not _is_int(score):
                continue
            if team_num == 0:
                snapshot.blue_score = score
            elif team_num == 1:
                snapshot.orange_score = score

    def _apply_players(
        self,
        snapshot: MatchStateSnapshot,
        players: object,
        game: dict[str, Any],
    ) -> None:
        """Rebuild the player list and resolve ``target_player``."""
        if not isinstance(players, list):
            snapshot.players = []
            snapshot.target_player = None
            return

        target_shortcut: int | None = None
        if game.get("bHasTarget"):
            target = game.get("Target")
            if isinstance(target, dict):
                raw_target = target.get("Shortcut")
                if _is_int(raw_target):
                    target_shortcut = raw_target

        result: list[PlayerSnapshot] = []
        target_player: PlayerSnapshot | None = None

        for entry in players:
            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
                continue
            player_snapshot = _build_player_snapshot(entry)
            if player_snapshot is None:
                continue
            result.append(player_snapshot)
            if target_player is None and player_snapshot.shortcut == target_shortcut:
                target_player = player_snapshot

        snapshot.players = result
        snapshot.target_player = target_player

    def _apply_goal_scored(
        self,
        snapshot: MatchStateSnapshot,
        data: dict[str, Any],
    ) -> None:
        """Update last scorer name and goal speed from a ``GoalScored`` payload."""
        scorer = data.get("Scorer")
        if isinstance(scorer, dict):
            name = scorer.get("Name")
            if isinstance(name, str) and name:
                snapshot.last_scorer = name

        goal_speed = data.get("GoalSpeed")
        if isinstance(goal_speed, (int, float)) and not isinstance(goal_speed, bool):
            snapshot.last_goal_speed = float(goal_speed)

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Since Rocket League v2.72 the game accepts commands on the same socket it uses to send events. StatsClient can send all six documented commands.

import asyncio
from rlstatsapi import StatsClient


async def main() -> None:
    async with StatsClient() as client:
        await client.wait_for("UpdateState")
        await client.set_hud_visibility(False)
        await client.change_pov(focus="Ball", perspective="Fly")


asyncio.run(main())

The game does not reply to commands, and it drops malformed ones without an error. For that reason every command is validated before it is written, and an invalid one raises InvalidCommandError (a ValueError). To confirm a command worked, watch the event stream: SetMatchPaused is followed by MatchPaused or MatchUnpaused, and LoadReplay by ReplayCreated.

Sending while disconnected raises ConnectionError.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text: Method Command Where it works change_pov(focus=None, perspective=None) ChangePOV Spectator, replay load_replay(file_name=None, path=None) LoadReplay Anywhere seek_replay(frame=None, time_seconds=None) SeekReplay Replay set_game_speed(speed) SetGameSpeed Replay set_hud_visibility(visible) SetHUDVisibility Anywhere set_match_paused(paused) SetMatchPaused Match or replay

docs.title: change_pov
docs.text:
At least one argument is required.

  • focus: "Ball", or a player's spectator shortcut as an int or a digit string. The shortcut is the Shortcut field of each player in UpdateState.
  • perspective: "Fly", "SoftAttach", "HardAttach", "PlayerView", "AutoCam" or "Camera_Director". When you focus a player and give no perspective, the game uses PlayerView.

docs.title: load_replay
docs.text: Pass file_name or path. If both are set the game uses file_name. The ReplayCreated event carries a FileName you can pass back here.

docs.title: seek_replay
docs.text: Pass frame or time_seconds. If both are set the game uses frame.

docs.title: set_game_speed
docs.text: 1.0 is normal speed, 0.5 half, 2.0 double. Must be 0 or greater.

docs.title: Raw envelopes
docs.text:
The wire format is {"Command": "<name>", "Data": {...}}. You can send it directly, by name or as a dict. Both forms go through the same validation.

await client.send_command("SetGameSpeed", {"Speed": 0.5})
await client.send_command({"Command": "SetMatchPaused", "Data": {"bPaused": True}})

The builders in rlstatsapi.commands return the envelope without sending it:

from rlstatsapi import commands, encode_command

envelope = commands.seek_replay(time_seconds=120.5)
payload = encode_command(envelope)  # b'{"Command":"SeekReplay","Data":{"TimeSeconds":120.5}}'

docs.title: From the CLI
docs.text:
rlstatsapi send SetHUDVisibility '{"bVisible": false}'
rlstatsapi send ChangePOV '{"Focus": "1", "Perspective": "PlayerView"}'

docs.title: Transport behavior
docs.text:
Since v2.72 the game opens two listeners: a plain TCP socket on Port (default 49123) and a WebSocket on WebPort (default 49124). rlstatsapi uses the TCP socket, which needs no extra dependency.

This means:

  • the client connects with a normal TCP socket
  • commands are written to that same socket
  • messages are decoded from a continuous JSON stream
  • Data can arrive either as a JSON object or as an escaped JSON string

docs.title: Platform scope
docs.text:
rlstatsapi itself is cross-platform Python code, but config discovery is currently Windows-first.

Automatic config helpers look for TAStatsAPI.ini in common user locations such as:

  • Documents\My Games\Rocket League\TAGame\Config
  • OneDrive\Documents\My Games\Rocket League\TAGame\Config
  • localized Documentos variants

If your setup lives somewhere else, pass an explicit path=... to the config helpers.

docs.title: Match data caveats
docs.text:
• MatchGuid is typically present only for online or LAN matches.
  • Some player fields are spectator-only and may be absent.
  • PacketSendRate must be greater than 0 to enable exporting.
  • BoostPickup and PickupClass are spectator-only.
  • GoalScored also fires during replay playback since v2.76.
  • MatchEnded.WinnerTeamNum is -1 when the match ends in no contest.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Automatic setup from Python:

from rlstatsapi import configure_stats_api

configure_stats_api(enabled=True, port=49123, packet_send_rate=30)

Or from the CLI:

rlstatsapi enable --port 49123 --rate 30
rlstatsapi disable
rlstatsapi status

Or manually by editing:

Documents\My Games\Rocket League\TAGame\Config\TAStatsAPI.ini

Recommended minimum:

[TAGame.MatchStatsExporter_TA]
Port=49123
WebPort=49124
PacketSendRate=30
Key Default Meaning PacketSendRate 0 UpdateState messages per second, up to 120. 0 disables the API. Port 49123 TCP port. This is the one StatsClient connects to. WebPort 49124 WebSocket port. 0 disables it. Must differ from Port.

To change the WebSocket port from Python:

from rlstatsapi import set_stats_api_web_port

set_stats_api_web_port(0)  # disable the WebSocket listener

Notes:

  • PacketSendRate > 0 enables exporting.
  • Restart Rocket League after changing the config file in either method.
  • Config discovery is currently Windows-first.
  • The game reads TAStatsAPI.ini and falls back to DefaultStatsAPI.ini. Discovery follows the same order.
  • The helpers refuse to write equal Port and WebPort values.
  • Use the same host and port in StatsClient.

from rlstatsapi.models import EventMessage

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Available scripts in examples/:

  • all_events_to_txt.py: log all events and persist changed payloads to a text file.
  • event_names_only.py: print event names as they arrive.
  • clock_updates.py: listen to ClockUpdatedSeconds and print the game clock.
  • goal_scored_typed.py: typed GoalScored handler with scorer name and speed.
  • configure_and_connect.py: configure the exporter and connect with the same port.
  • match_lifecycle.py: track the full match lifecycle from creation to destruction.
  • decorator_handlers.py: register handlers using the decorator form of client.on().
  • statfeed_events.py: print StatfeedEvent highlights - saves, shots, demos, etc.

docs.title: Typed payload pattern (Pylance-friendly)
docs.text:
from rlstatsapi.models import EventMessage
from rlstatsapi.types import GoalScoredPayload, cast_event_data


def on_goal(msg: EventMessage) -> None:
    data: GoalScoredPayload = cast_event_data("GoalScored", msg.data)
    scorer = data.get("Scorer", {})
    print(scorer.get("Name"))

Why this pattern:

  • StatsClient.on(...) handlers receive EventMessage
  • cast_event_data(...) narrows to the event-specific payload type
  • no runtime validation overhead
